Truckers block roads in Chile protesting fuel price hikes

SANTIAGO, Nov 10 (Reuters) – Truck drivers across Chile staged strikes and blockades on Tuesday to protest sustained fuel price increases linked to global geopolitical volatility, disrupting traffic along the country’s key north-south highway and access to ports including Iquique.

The stoppage was called by Chile’s ‘Confederacion de Transportistas Fuerza del Norte’ and the ‘No+TAG’ movement, which expected to gather around 4,000 truckers, though the sector’s two largest associations declined to join.

• Protesters are demanding government measures to contain fuel prices, changes to the MEPCO fuel-price stabilization mechanism, and modifications to the tax burden on truckers

Show Full Article

• The government said on Monday it would seek to use fiscal savings to support MEPCO

• It also plans to send a bill to prevent weekly fuel price increases of more than 20 pesos ($0.02) per liter

• A cruise ship canceled a planned stop in Iquique due to the potential impact of protests, according to Diario Financiero newspaper

($1 = 967.0000 Chilean pesos)

(Reporting by Fabian Cambero; writing by Aida Pelaez-Fernandez)
